reconstructed_theorem_text: Definition. For any finite type I, let S={w in EuclideanSpace R I: ||w||=1}, let u:NNReal->S->EuclideanSpace R I and a:NNReal->R be arbitrary functions. Given i in I, t>=0 and w in S, the defined real value is coordinate i of -u(t,w)-(a(t)*k)*w, namely -u_i(t,w)-a(t)*k*w_i, where k is the real cast of the natural-number subtraction card(I)-1. The subtype value w is included in the ambient Euclidean space. No measurability, continuity, sign, tangency, or boundedness condition is required.
objects: Finite coordinate type I, sphere S, vector field u, scalar function a, i,t,w, real scalar output.
domains: u on NNReal times and the unit sphere of EuclideanSpace R I; a real-valued; i in I.
quantifiers: For every finite I, every u and a, then every i,t,w, the definition supplies the displayed scalar.
assumptions: Only the stated types and finite-type instance.
scopes: Pointwise formula on all nonnegative times and all sphere points.
constant_dependencies: Depends on u,a,i,t,w and dimension factor with natural subtraction; no existential constant.
context_ambiguities: None identified from the supplied statement and definition context.
